newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat urges world to defend Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Arafat urges world to defend Palestinians.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat urged the world to move to save Palestinians from Israel's "collective punishment" measures, the Arab League said on Monday.

It said the plea was made in a letter sent by Arafat to Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid following Israel's punitive measures against Palestinians in retaliation to a double suicide bombing in West Jerusalem last week.
Permanent representatives to the Cairo-based Arab League will hold an extraordinary session on Tuesday at the request of the Palestinians to discuss the latest crisis in Middle East peace efforts.

"Arab League Secretary-General Esmat Abdel-Meguid received a letter from...Arafat, who asked for necessary actions on the Arab and international arena to save the Palestinian people from the latest Israeli collective punishment measures," the League statement said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's cabinet has demanded Arafat crack down on Moslem militants behind last week's suicide bombings that killed 13 people and wounded 170.

Israel also suspended peace talks with the Palestinians, rounded up scores of suspected militants, closed off the West Bank and Gaza Strip, demanded the extradition of the PLO police chief and threatened to re-enter Palestinian self-rule areas to seize militants if Arafat failed to do the job.

In his letter, Arafat mentioned 12 measures taken by Israel after the bombing, including stopping the transfer of tax and other funds to the Palestinian Authority, banning the movement of ambulances and doctors' vehicles and preventing Palestinian fishermen from sailing in the territorial waters of Gaza.
"Those measures were taken despite the Palestinian Authority's condemnation of the latest terrorist operation," the League said.

"The letter renewed the Palestinian rejection of terrorism in all its forms and urged the secretary general to move quickly to put an end to this deterioration and to save the peace process," it added.
